Notes
• LoRa selling price INR 1,600 (owner, 2026-11-19), read as price after profit without battery board and adapter: needs
a BOM of ≤ INR 687 at 100 pcs, now 1,109 — a 38 % cut.
• With Ethernet, incl. power stage and enclosure: 3,670 (limit INR 2,000: over by 1,670); the version without Ethernet
is dropped (owner, 2026-11-19).
• PIC32CK2051SG01 is the standard MCU for now (owner, 2026-11-19). Open points: no PSA / SESIP certificate (BASE-1 not
met); Zephyr has no PIC32CK Ethernet, CAN or ADC driver yet (R12) — drivers to write or ThreadX; STM32H573 stays as
the alternative.
• LoRa redesigned as a remote IO node (owner, 2026-11-19): STM32WLE5 at INR 250, 2-layer PCB, no external flash, RS-485
+ 4 DI + 4 AI + 4 DO (low-power high-side quad), SMA antenna kept for long range — BOM 1,109. Tip: volume quotes (≈
−10 %) → ≈ 998; no relays: their coils would drain the battery.
• Tip — every module: this is a high-volume product, so negotiate the big parts with distributors (modem, ESP32-C6
module, MCUs, isolated transceivers, enclosures); the BOMs here are still research prices × 1.3 at 100 units.
• Adapter (owner, 2026-11-18): one 12 V 18 W adapter per stack or standalone module; a full 4-module stack peaks at ≈
13–14 W with charging capped at 0.3 A per battery board.
• Not included: development amortisation — at 100 pieces every INR 1 lakh of NRE per module type adds INR 1,000 to its
cost and ≈ INR 1,300 to its price after profit; distributor margin (left to the client / partner).
